title: Imaging coupled filtering: A unified multi-channel framework for multimodal medical image registration and fusion

aimed_contribution.improvement: Effectively addresses insufficient image decomposition, preserving and enhancing multi-feature expression of source images
aimed_contribution.implementation_detail: Refines source images into four coupling channels (smoothing, texture, contour, and edge) and incorporates association and coupling of each feature channel.
aimed_contribution.improve_from: Existing frequency domain methods with deficiencies in feature loss and insufficient color restoration

aimed_contribution.improvement: Better maintenance of overall image structure and significant enrichment of multi-feature expression and structural similarity between fused and source images
aimed_contribution.implementation_detail: Proposes a visual saliency decomposition strategy and a visual saliency based NSCT fusion rule.

aimed_contribution.improvement: Accurate distinction of detail levels in adhesive lesion invasion areas by extracting detail and hierarchical information from image space and intensity aspects
Provides robust data support for subsequent image fusion research
aimed_contribution.implementation_detail: Acquired, desensitized, and registered 403 groups of multimodal abdominal medical images (Ab-MI) and made them publicly available.
aimed_contribution.improve_from: Lack of open-source benchmark datasets at the systemic level

datasets.details: 403 groups of multimodal abdominal medical images (Ab-MI) collected across four imaging modalities and five disease categories. Contains 74 groups of MR-T1/MR-T2 image pairs from three patients, and 329 groups of CT/PET image pairs from two other patients. All images are 256x256 resolution. Registered using FourierNet-based method.
Publicly available dataset for brain images, comprising 59 groups of CT/MR image pairs and 86 groups of MR/PET image pairs. All images are 256x256 resolution.

experiment_setup.training_details: All experiments are implemented in Matlab 2018a with AMD Ryzen 7 5800 and Radeon Graphics 3.20GHz, 16G RAM. No specific training details for a deep learning model are provided as ICF is a traditional method.
